headline.text: Pohjanmaa's crude curative treatment share is 27.8% (95% CI 23.9–32.2; n=125/449) versus 27.0% nationally, with the 95% confidence interval including the national value while pathway wait times remain unmeasured.

details.text: Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can have several, Pohjanmaa's crude curative share is 27.8% (95% CI 23.9–32.2; n=125/449) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally and crude symptomatic treatment is 36.1% (95% CI 31.8–40.6; n=162/449) versus 39.5% (5871/14873), with each 95% confidence interval including the national value.

Pohjanmaa's crude life-prolonging treatment share is 43.0% (95% CI 38.5–47.6; n=193/449), whose 95% confidence interval excludes the national 30.4% (4522/14873) above it, while crude MDT meeting recording is 6.9% (95% CI 4.9–9.6; n=31/449) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with its 95% confidence interval including the national value.

MDT records measure recording practice rather than care because HILMO captures specialist procedures only from direct patient contacts, and while county wait times are unmeasured, preliminary national figures average 155 days from symptoms to treatment in Finland (56 days patient delay, 41 days primary care, 58 days specialist care) versus 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark.

headline.text: Pohjanmaa's crude 22.9% (95% CI 19.3–27.1; n=103/449) share with no treatment record within 12 months excludes the national 27.5%, while public data lack stage and pathway timestamps.

details.text: Because the 95% confidence interval for Pohjanmaa's crude 22.9% (95% CI 19.3–27.1; n=103/449) share with no treatment record within 12 months excludes the national 27.5% (4089/14873)—a category mixing untreated patients and unrecorded treatment—we infer this data-quality signal is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording, though not direct evidence of it.

All reported county treatment shares are crude and not adjusted for age or stage: stage at diagnosis is missing for ~48% of new patients, and Kuva 16 (digitised from a figure, precision ±0.5 percentage points, for curative treatment only by sex) provides only the national age-adjusted reference lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women.

A 2019 Lääkärilehti journal article found HILMO diagnoses matched the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, concerning diagnosis concordance only and not treatment or MDT recording, while public data do not measure symptom onset, referral dates, imaging waits (diagnosis rests on clinical examination alone in approximately 20%), or when treatment started.

Outpatient primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned despite mentor insight that occupational health gets patients to specialist care faster and a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating, and HILMO shows 93.6% had a specialist visit within 12 months (up to 3 months pre-diagnosis) without visit dates.

headline.text: The team recommends reporting THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 access times with handover alerts, standardising referrals with a diagnostic contact, and publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT.

details.text: The team recommends reporting access times from referral to first specialist visit, diagnosis, and treatment start using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions (for 16 cancers) and flagging stalled handovers, because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for cancer suspicion, national pathway access times are planned for 2026–2028, and Filha's diagnostic time limits are due before 2030.

The team recommends a standard referral list and template modelled on the KYS regional pathway document, referring persistent symptoms after a clear X-ray to a pulmonologist, and naming a diagnostic contact person, since referrals follow local instructions, mentor insight notes weak referrals get lower urgency, and national referral criteria and coordinator guidance are planned for 2026–2028 (county adoption 2029–2031).

The team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding and reading gaps as data-quality signals, since stage is missing for ~48% of patients nationally, Pohjanmaa's crude MDT recording is 6.9% (95% CI 4.9–9.6; n=31/449; 95% CI includes national 6.0%, 893/14873), data collection is incomplete, and a planned national quality registry targets 90% coverage.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
rec:3.location: §3. Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding
